summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard; the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 gives it 85 ft and 125 ft height limits, and its build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation. The October 2026 height ordinance's map labels the block 93 ft and 133 ft, but the block is in the PG&E Sub-Area, where the zoning controls (the 2020 limits as well as the new ones) are not operative until a Notice of Joinder to the Development Agreement is recorded or the land is conveyed to the Developer; no source read shows either, so on the sources read neither set of limits has taken effect on this land. The Board of Supervisors approved the project and Development Agreement on April 21, 2020 (Ordinance No. 62-20; the agreement's effective date is May 25, 2020).

details.text: Standard 6.2.2 of the D4D lists Block 13 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft); the adopted plan's 85 ft and 125 ft labels (Figure 6.2.3) sit within that range.

Enacted heights on Block 13 and when they become operative: the enacted height map (BOS File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29, Figure 249.87-2) labels Block 13 "93'" and "133'" (its "300'MAX" and "280'MAX" labels are dimension lines, not heights); the adopted D4D's labels are 85 ft and 125 ft. The map is read from the rendered page, whose text layer is unreliable, so the labels were read by eye. The replacement Map 249.87-1 (p. 54; the earlier map on p. 53 is struck through) labels the area "PG&E Sub-Area" (the map prints it in capitals) west of Georgia Street, the same outline in which Figure 249.87-2 labels Block 13 (compared by eye); Block 14 is east of Georgia Street, outside it. Section 5(c) (p. 56) reads: "this ordinance shall not become operative as to the areas labeled as "PG&E Sub-Area" on Map 249.87-1, or any portion thereof, until the conditions in Section 249.87(t) have been satisfied." Section 249.87(t), 'Operative Date for the PG&E Sub-Area' (p. 52), reads: "The zoning controls expressed in this Section 249.87 shall not become operative as to the PG&E Sub-Area, as shown on Map 249.87-1, or any portion thereof, until a Notice of Joinder to the Development Agreement has been recorded, or until the PG&E Sub-Area, or any portion thereof, is conveyed to the Developer." (The words "approved by the Board of Supervisors in Board file No. 200040" after "Development Agreement" are struck through in the enacted text.) The rest of the ordinance becomes operative on the later of its own effective date and File 260724's (File 260770 §5(b), p. 56; File 260724 §7(b), p. 10); each takes effect on the 31st day after enactment (§5(a); §7(a)), and both were enacted Oct 13, 2026 per Legistar, so the other Potrero blocks' limits take effect Nov 13, 2026 by our count, a legal date computed by Pier & Point and not printed in the text. That date does not apply to Block 13. Section 249.87(t) is existing Code text, not a new addition (p. 52 shows it without underlining; only the words about Board file No. 200040 are struck), so the adopted 2020 limits of 85 ft and 125 ft were subject to the same condition: they were not operative on this land either.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 13; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

Corrected 2026-09-29: an earlier version of this dossier read the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on Figure 6.2.3 as heights and reported a conflict with Standard 6.2.2; they are dimension lines (plan extents), and the block's heights are 85 ft and 125 ft, within the midrise range. The D4D's Appendix A.12 is titled 'Block 13 Controls (Low-rise Building)' while Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 as midrise (101-145 ft); the difference in labels is unexplained.
Block 13's 2031-2035 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite) and is contingent on the PG&E switchyard's relocation; no current Block 13 schedule was found.

DataSF Parcels lists an active addressed lot (4175499, 1101 Illinois St) over this block's approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established, and whether this record's map shape should follow it has not been decided.

Block 13's enacted heights (93 ft and 133 ft, File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29) are not yet operative: Block 13 is in the PG&E Sub-Area, and Section 249.87(t) (p. 52) says the zoning controls "shall not become operative as to the PG&E Sub-Area ... or any portion thereof, until a Notice of Joinder to the Development Agreement has been recorded, or until the PG&E Sub-Area, or any portion thereof, is conveyed to the Developer" (Section 5(c), p. 56, says the same of the ordinance). The Nov 13, 2026 effective date that applies to the other Potrero blocks does not apply here. Section 249.87(t) is existing text (p. 52), so the adopted 85 ft and 125 ft limits were subject to the same condition and, on the sources read, were never operative on this land. No source read shows a Notice of Joinder recorded or the land conveyed: SF Planning's project page (undated; read Oct 18, 2026) still says the switchyard parcel is "currently owned and operated by PG&E" and that build-out "will depend on the relocation of the switchyard and the property coming within the legal jurisdiction of the Development Agreement", and File 260724's recital (d) (p. 2) says PG&E "owns approximately 3.8 acres" in the PG&E Sub-Area. The County Recorder's records were not searched. The 3.8 acres in that recital differs from the 4.8 acres on SF Planning's page; the difference is not explained in the sources read.
